resources.string: Every paper you keep, found in seconds.
Find anything: every word on every page is searchable.
Plain PDFs you own, in a folder you choose.
I already use No Papers Needed on another device
A plain folder you can open in any file manager. You can sync it to other devices later.
Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box, pCloud or Nextcloud. Sign in and pick a folder; this device keeps a copy, so it works offline too.
More providers are in Settings under Cloud sync, once your library is open.
Your library is a folder. Choose how this device reaches it; nothing in it changes until it opens.
Sign in to the cloud drive your other device syncs to, and pick the library’s folder there.
A folder a sync app keeps up to date
Syncthing, the Nextcloud app or a similar tool: let it bring the library folder to this device first, then choose that folder.
A folder already on this device
A library on this device’s storage, a USB drive or a memory card.
This device then reads every file once to find your documents; you will see how far it has got.
Which languages are your documents in?
Text recognition reads scanned pages in these languages. Each one more makes it a little slower; you can change them later in Settings under Import & text recognition.
Checking which languages this computer can read…
Everything needed for these languages is included with the app.
Text recognition needs Tesseract, which is not installed yet.
Install Tesseract’s language data for %1$s with your system’s package manager.
A bill, a letter, a receipt: anything you want to find again. It goes into your library as a plain PDF.
Or drop PDF files anywhere on this window
This takes a few seconds a page. You can open the document meanwhile.
Its text is read: you can search for any word on its pages.
That document was already in your library.
Here is your first document. To find it again, search the library for a word from its page.
Here is your first document. Once its text is read, search the library for a word from its page to find it again.
No documents yet. If a sync app is still copying the folder, they appear as they arrive.
You can start now: this carries on in the background.
Connect to your own Nextcloud, ownCloud or another WebDAV server.
The address you open in your browser, such as cloud.example.com
With two-step sign-in, create an app password in your server’s security settings and use that.
Use this library on a phone, a laptop or both: how to get it there.
Your library is a folder. Another device can use it as soon as that folder reaches it; each device then builds its own index from the files.
On the other device, install No Papers Needed and choose “I already use No Papers Needed on another device”, then “From my cloud drive”. Sign in there and pick %1$s.
Connect this library to a cloud drive under Cloud sync first. Then, on the other device, choose “I already use No Papers Needed on another device” and pick the same cloud folder.
Share %1$s with the other device in Syncthing. Once it has arrived there, choose “I already use No Papers Needed on another device”, then the synced folder.
Keep %1$s in a folder the Nextcloud desktop app syncs, and let it sync to the other computer too; then choose that folder there. On a phone, connect to Nextcloud as a cloud drive instead.
This library’s files are kept in the app’s own storage, which sync apps cannot reach: add devices through its cloud folder.
It reads every file once to find your documents and shows how far it has got, such as “Reading files (12 of 340)…”. Documents appear as they are read, with their tags and details.
No sign-in travels from this device: each device signs in on its own.
